identity.title: AI Security Engineer
identity.heroDescription: Working toward securing AI applications, RAG systems and tool-using agents through practical learning and evidence-based security engineering.
identity.about: I’m Ahmed, an aspiring AI Security Engineer focused on AI Application & Product Security. My goal is to develop the skills to protect AI applications, retrieval-augmented generation systems and tool-using agents. My learning plan emphasizes authorization, data privacy, prompt injection, secure tool execution, security evaluation and reliable operations. I aim to turn this work into reproducible case studies that explain the problem, the control, the evidence and the remaining limitations.

metadata.title: Ahmed Amhdour — AI Security Engineer
metadata.description: Ahmed Amhdour’s AI security portfolio: planned case studies in AI application security, RAG security, agent security, evaluation, privacy and secure operations.
metadata.socialDescription: Evidence-first AI security learning portfolio focused on AI applications, RAG systems and tool-using agents.

focusAreas.title: AI application authorization and privacy
focusAreas.description: Learning to trace identity, object ownership, session state, revocation and sensitive-data flows so authority stays at the responsible service boundary.

focusAreas.title: RAG ingestion, retrieval and data lifecycle
focusAreas.description: Studying provenance, permission-aware retrieval, stale access, memory boundaries, deletion and the lifecycle of derived copies such as indexes and caches.

focusAreas.title: MCP, agent permissions and secure tool execution
focusAreas.description: Focusing on user-scoped consent, task-bound authority, exact approvals, destination policy, retries, idempotency and independently verifiable effects.

focusAreas.title: Prompt-injection and security regression evaluation
focusAreas.description: Designing bounded attack and legitimate-task cases, effect-level oracles, evaluator validation and repeatable release gates without treating model self-reports as ground truth.

focusAreas.title: Secure delivery, telemetry and incident recovery
focusAreas.description: Connecting provenance, audit events, detection, containment, rollback, reconciliation and handover so controls remain understandable after change or failure.

learningJourney.intro: Mission IDs are stable learning references, not months or fixed completion dates. Progress advances when prerequisites and evidence gates are satisfied.

foundation.title: Threat model and security requirements
foundation.description: Establish the system boundary, assets, authority transitions, threats, testable requirements and evidence plan before adding specialized work.

foundation.title: API ownership and authorization
foundation.description: Trace caller, object and action checks; compare permitted and denied cases; distinguish ordinary ownership from sharing, administration and tenancy.

foundation.title: Secure uploads and file handling
foundation.description: Study size and parser boundaries, ownership, failure cleanup, artifact state and recoverability while keeping fixtures bounded and synthetic.

foundation.title: Configuration and secrets
foundation.description: Map listeners, privileges, secrets, destinations, rotation and effective configuration before making runtime or isolation claims.

foundation.title: Data-flow and privacy analysis
foundation.description: Trace sensitive fields to model, tool and log sinks, define minimization rules and verify allowed and denied data flows with deterministic evidence.

tracks.title: Application & Product Security
tracks.description: Authorization, data and action boundaries; secure delivery, operations, durable security tooling and supplier decisions.
tracks.prerequisite: Build on M01–M05 and the specific identity, data or action prerequisites of each mission.

tracks.title: Agent Application Security
tracks.missions: Relevant M01–M30 foundations, then M34; M38/M39 when required
tracks.description: Peer identity, delegation, approvals, effect containment and safe stopping; add computer-use or malicious-use controls only when the target responsibility needs them.
tracks.prerequisite: Requires the applicable authorization, MCP/action and incident-evidence foundations before peer or executor claims.

tracks.title: Model & Training Security
tracks.description: Robustness, training/artifact trust and model-privacy experiments grounded in known synthetic data and held-out evaluation.
tracks.prerequisite: Requires ML/statistics foundations, a pinned real small model or trainer, valid splits and a declared attacker/output contract.

tracks.title: Inference Platform Security
tracks.description: Serving-engine management, worker, artifact and cache boundaries when an actual engine and suitable resources are available.
tracks.prerequisite: Native runtime evidence is gated on the selected engine/build, hardware/resources and actual management/worker/cache architecture.

tracks.title: Security Program Ownership
tracks.description: Evidence-backed intake, decisions, maintenance, recurrence prevention and cross-product operating practice.
tracks.prerequisite: Senior production ownership is not created by a synthetic exercise; real responsibility requires real accountable roles and operating evidence.
